title: The Easter vigil
hookLine: a fire, a great candle, and an ancient song, the Exsultet: this is the night

lines: ONE TALL CANDLE IN THE DARK.
cards: Saturday night, after dark, and the church is pitch black. Outside the door a small fire burns, and people stand around it in their coats.
A tall candle is lit from the fire and carried in, and a voice sings out: the light of Christ. The people answer: thanks be to God.

The flame is passed from the tall candle, hand to hand, until the dark room is full of small lights. Then someone sings an old song called the Exsultet, and one line keeps coming back in it. This is the night.

teach.b: A vigil is a night spent awake, waiting. This one waits for Easter, and it starts in the dark on purpose. The Exsultet opens by calling heaven and earth to rejoice.
Then it turns into a list, and line after line begins: this is the night. This is the night, it sings, when God brought Israel out of Egypt and through the sea.
This is the night when a pillar of fire drove back the darkness. This is the night when Christ broke the chains of death and rose.

teach.h: A NIGHT TO BE MUCH OBSERVED.
teach.b: The song reaches back to Exodus, which says of the night Israel left Egypt, in the King James: "It is a night to be much observed unto the LORD for bringing them out from the land of Egypt."

Jewish families keep that night at the Passover table with their own telling of the story. The vigil takes up the same night and sets the empty tomb inside it. Then the Exsultet says something daring.
It calls Adam's sin a happy fault, because of the rescue it led to: yesterday's icon, sung.
After the song, in churches that keep the full vigil, story after story from the Hebrew Bible is read by candlelight: creation, the sea, the prophets. Then the church fills with light.

teach.h: LIGHTS UP, AND THE ALLELUIA BACK.
teach.b: In churches that set the alleluia aside for Lent, it comes back tonight. Some churches baptize new Christians at this service.
And the candle carries a line from John's Gospel into the room: "And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not."

how: Catholics, Anglicans, Lutherans and some other churches keep the Easter Vigil on Saturday night: a new fire, the Easter candle carried into the dark church, the Exsultet sung, readings from the Hebrew Bible, and sometimes baptisms.

games.q: you're holding an unlit candle in a dark church. the tall candle comes past. what happens?
o: you wait for the lights to come on.
the flame is passed from the tall candle, hand to hand, to yours.
you light your own with a match.
games.why: the light spreads from the one candle, person to person, until the whole dark room is full of small flames.

practice: Turn off as many lights as you can and light one candle somewhere safe, or use the smallest light you have. Watch how far one small flame reaches, the edges of the room you can and can't see.
If you pray, say the vigil's line quietly, this is the night; if not, simply stay with the one light and the dark around it.

wordCard.voice: Exsultet. The ancient song sung by candlelight at the Easter vigil, repeating this is the night as it tells the story of rescue.

orig.note: Latin: this is the night — the refrain of the Exsultet.

carryVoice: Your line: this is the night. One flame, then a room full. Until tomorrow.
